title: An open group-homomorphism image over a field is closed
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], and let $u:P\to Q$ be a homomorphism of group schemes over $\operatorname{Spec}k$ [def-sc-group-scheme, def-pc-scheme, def-weil-affine-spectrum]. A group scheme here is a scheme over $k$ with multiplication, inverse and identity satisfying the group diagrams, and a homomorphism respects these morphisms. If the point image $u(|P|)$ is open in the underlying topological space $|Q|$, then $u(|P|)$ is closed in $|Q|$. No finite-type, smoothness, separatedness, affineness, injectivity or surjectivity hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Tag 047S, lemma-open-subgroup-closed-over-field, statement and translation proof.

proof.text: A group scheme over $\operatorname{Spec}k$ gives an absolute groupoid scheme by taking the object scheme to be $V=\operatorname{Spec}k$, the arrow scheme to be the group scheme, and both source and target maps to be its structure morphism. The unit, inverse and composition are the group unit, inverse and multiplication; the group axioms imply the groupoid diagrams. A homomorphism of group schemes, together with $\mathrm{id}_V$, commutes with these operations. Thus the given image is the image of a morphism of the absolute groupoid schemes in the existing open-image lemma.

source.place: Tag 0234 (lemma-groupoid-from-action) with Y = X = Spec k and the trivial action: U = Spec k, R = G, s = t = structure morphism, c = m, e = e_G, i = i_G.

proof.text: Apply `lem-sfb-field-groupoid-open-image-closed` to the two groupoid schemes and their morphism from Step 1. Its hypotheses are exactly satisfied, and it says that the image of the morphism is closed whenever it is open. Therefore $u(|P|)$ is closed in $|Q|$.
